title.zh: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁
title.en: Volume 464 Biographies 251: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijingzi, Ren Zhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Ceng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong With: Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, Kang Guangren
title.raw: 卷464 列傳二百五十一 李端棻 徐致靖子 仁铸 陈宝箴 黄遵宪 曾鉌 杨深秀 杨锐 刘光第 谭嗣同附：唐才常 林旭 康广仁

sentences.zh: 李端棻 徐致靖 子仁鑄 陳寶箴 黃遵憲 曾鉌 楊深秀 楊銳 劉光第 譚嗣同 唐才常 林旭 康廣仁 李端棻，字苾園，貴州貴筑人。

translations.literal: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing, son Renzhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Zeng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, courtesy name Biyuan, was a native of Guizhu in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing, his son Renzhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Zeng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, whose courtesy name was Biyuan, came from Guizhu in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為大學士倭仁、尚書羅敦衍所器。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi year two he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler, appointed compiler, and was valued by Grand Secretary Woren and Minister Luo Dunyan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, was appointed a compiler, and won the regard of Grand Secretary Woren and Minister Luo Dunyan.

sentences.zh: 十年，出督雲南學政。

translations.literal: In year ten, he was sent out as Educational Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten he was sent out as Educational Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 值回寇亂後，荒服道亙，前使者試未遍，端棻始一一按臨，文化漸振。

translations.literal: This was after the Muslim uprising, when frontier routes were still broken and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations throughout the province. Duanfen now toured each district in person, and culture and learning gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: This was after the Muslim uprising, when frontier routes were still broken and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations throughout the province. Duanfen toured each district in person, and learning gradually revived.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，轉御史，以叔父朝儀官京尹，迴避，改故官。

translations.literal: In Guangxu year five he was transferred to censor, but because his uncle Chaoyi held office as metropolitan magistrate of Beijing, he withdrew under the avoidance rule and returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 5 he was made a censor, but when his uncle Chaoyi served as metropolitan magistrate of Beijing, he withdrew under the kinship rule and resumed his former office.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to junior grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to junior grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was moved to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 越六年，調倉場。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was reassigned to oversee the grain depots.

sentences.zh: 前後迭司文柄，四為鄉試考官，一為會試副總裁，喜獎拔士類。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly held control of literary examinations: four times as examiner for the provincial examinations and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination; he delighted in rewarding and promoting men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: On several occasions he held charge of the civil examinations, serving four times as provincial examiner and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination, and he took pleasure in recognizing and advancing promising scholars.

sentences.zh: 典試廣東，賞梁啟超才，以從妹妻之，自是頗納啟超議，娓娓道東西邦制度。

translations.literal: While conducting examinations in Guangdong he admired Liang Qichao's ability and married a younger female cousin to him; thereafter he often accepted Qichao's counsel and spoke at length about the institutions of Eastern and Western countries.
translations.idiomatic: While conducting examinations in Guangdong he admired Liang Qichao's ability, married a younger female cousin to him, and thereafter often took Liang's counsel, speaking at length about the political systems of East and West.

sentences.zh: 維時康有為上書請變法，兼及興學。

translations.literal: At this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials requesting reform, also touching on the promotion of schools.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials calling for reform and for the expansion of education.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，端棻遂疏請立京師大學，凡各省府、州、縣遍設學堂，分齋講習；

translations.literal: In year twenty-two, Duanfen then memorialized requesting the establishment of a capital university, and that schools be set up throughout every province, prefecture, department, and county, with halls divided for instruction and practice;
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two Duanfen memorialized to establish a national university in the capital and schools in every province, prefecture, department, and county, with separate halls for study;

sentences.zh: 並建藏書樓、儀器院、譯書局，廣立報館，選派遊歷生。

translations.literal: and also to build libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, to establish newspapers widely, and to select and send students abroad for observation.
translations.idiomatic: and to set up libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, to open newspapers widely, and to select students to travel abroad for study.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，密薦康有為及譚嗣同堪大用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as men capable of high responsibility.

sentences.zh: 又以各衙門則例，語涉紛歧，疏請刪訂，上尤善之，詔趣各長官定限期革前敝。

translations.literal: He also noted that the regulations of the various yamens were worded in conflicting ways and memorialized requesting their revision; the emperor especially approved this and ordered each chief official to set a deadline for abolishing former abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He further observed that the regulatory precedents of the various offices were inconsistent in wording and asked that they be revised; the emperor was especially pleased and ordered each department head to fix a deadline for removing old abuses.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有為等敗，端棻自疏檢舉，詔褫職，戍新疆。

translations.literal: Before long Kang Youwei and his associates were ruined; Duanfen memorialized accusing himself, and an edict stripped him of office and sent him into exile in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kang Youwei's party fell; Duanfen submitted a memorial denouncing himself, and an edict removed him from office and banished him to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 中道遘疾，留甘州。

translations.literal: On the way he fell ill and was detained at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill en route and was held at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，赦歸，主講貴州經世學堂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was pardoned and returned home, where he served as lecturer at the Guizhou Jingshi Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was amnestied and went home, where he lectured at the Guizhou Jingshi Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he died.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，從雲南、貴州京朝官請，復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, at the request of officials from Yunnan and Guizhou in the capital, his former office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong, at the petition of Yunnan and Guizhou officials in Beijing, his former office was restored.

sentences.zh: 徐致靖，字子靜，江蘇宜興人，寄籍宛平。

translations.literal: Xu Zhijing, courtesy name Zijing, was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu, with registered domicile at Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijing, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Yixing in Jiangsu and was registered at Wanping.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 父憂服闋，二十三年，起故官。

translations.literal: When his mourning for his father was completed, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 致靖嘗憂外患日迫，思所以為獻納計。

translations.literal: Zhijing had long been troubled by foreign pressure growing daily more urgent and pondered how he might offer advice to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing had long been troubled by the daily tightening of foreign pressure and pondered how he might advise the throne.

sentences.zh: 子仁鑄，時以編修督湘學，倡新學，書告致靖舉康有為。

translations.literal: His son Renzhu, then a compiler serving as educational commissioner of Hunan, promoted the new learning and wrote telling Zhijing to recommend Kang Youwei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renzhu, then a compiler serving as Hunan's educational commissioner, promoted the new learning and wrote urging Zhijing to recommend Kang Youwei.

sentences.zh: 致靖遂上言：「國是未定，請申乾斷示從違。」

translations.literal: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I request that Your Majesty's own judgment be made explicit, showing what is to be adopted and what rejected."
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I ask that Your Majesty's own judgment be made explicit, showing what is to be adopted and what rejected."

sentences.zh: 藉以覘上意。

translations.literal: Thus he sought to gauge the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he hoped to discern the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔果求通才，於是致靖奏有為堪大用，並及梁啟超、黃遵憲等。

translations.literal: Before long an edict indeed called for men of broad ability; Zhijing then memorialized that Youwei was fit for great employment, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict did call for broadly talented men; Zhijing then reported that Kang Youwei was fit for high office, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 又連上書請廢製藝，改試策論，省冗官，酌置散卿。

translations.literal: He also submitted successive memorials requesting the abolition of the examination essay, replacement by policy discourse, reduction of superfluous offices, and the considered establishment of honorary grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a series of memorials asking to abolish the eight-legged essay, test policy essays instead, cut redundant offices, and appoint honorary grand secretaries as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 復以邊患棘，宜練重兵，力荐袁世凱主軍事。

translations.literal: He further urged that with border troubles urgent, heavy forces should be trained, and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to direct military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He further urged that with border crises pressing, large forces should be drilled, and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to direct military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上皆然其言，敕依行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them implemented.

sentences.zh: 罷斥禮部尚書許應騤等阻遏言路，遂命致靖權右侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who had obstructed the channels of remonstrance were removed, and Zhijing was appointed acting right vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who had obstructed memorials to the throne were removed, and Zhijing was appointed acting right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 二十四年八月，太后復出訓政，參預新政諸臣皆獲罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed regency, and all the officials who had taken part in the new policies were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed control of government, and every official who had joined the reform movement was punished.

sentences.zh: 致靖褫職坐系，尋定永遠監禁，仁鑄亦罷官。

translations.literal: Zhijing was stripped of office and imprisoned; soon he was sentenced to lifelong detention, and Renzhu was also dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing was stripped of rank and imprisoned; he was soon sentenced to lifelong detention, and Renzhu was dismissed from office as well.

sentences.zh: 庚子，聯軍陷京師，致靖始出獄待罪，詔赦免。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies occupied the capital, Zhijing was first released from prison to await sentence, and an edict granted him amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies occupied Beijing, Zhijing was released from prison to await sentence, and an edict granted him amnesty.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 陳寶箴，字右銘，江西義寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Baozhen, courtesy name Youming, was from Yining in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen, courtesy name Youming, was from Yining in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 少負志節，詩文皆有法度，為曾國籓所器。

translations.literal: From youth he showed strong character; his poetry and prose were disciplined, and Zeng Guofan valued him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed strong character; his poetry and prose were disciplined, and Zeng Guofan valued him.

sentences.zh: 以舉人隨父偉琳治鄉團，禦粵寇。

translations.literal: While still a provincial graduate, he followed his father Weilin in managing local militia against the Guangdong rebels.
translations.idiomatic: While still a provincial graduate, he followed his father Weilin in managing local militia against the Guangdong rebels.

sentences.zh: 已而走湖南，參易佩紳戎幕，軍來鳳、龍山間。

translations.literal: He then went to Hunan, entered Yi Peishen’s military staff, and campaigned between Laifeng and Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Hunan, entered Yi Peishen’s military staff, and campaigned between Laifeng and Longshan.

sentences.zh: 石達開來犯，軍飢疲，走永順募糧，糧至不絕，守益堅，寇稍稍引去。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai attacked, the troops were hungry and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept coming, the defense held firmer, and the rebels gradually withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai attacked, the troops were hungry and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept coming, the defense held firmer, and the rebels gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 寶箴之江西，為席寶田畫策殲寇洪福瑱，事寧，敘知府，超授河北道。

translations.literal: When Baozhen went to Jiangxi, he planned for Xi Baotian the destruction of the rebel Hong Fuzhen; when matters were pacified, he was recommended as prefect and promoted out of turn to intendant of Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen went to Jiangxi, he planned for Xi Baotian the destruction of the rebel Hong Fuzhen; when matters were pacified, he was recommended as prefect and promoted out of turn to intendant of Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 創致用精舍，遴選三州學子，延名師教之。

translations.literal: He founded the Zhiyong Jingshe Academy, selected students from three prefectures, and invited distinguished teachers to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Zhiyong Jingshe Academy, selected students from three prefectures, and invited distinguished teachers to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江按察使，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be judicial commissioner of Zhejiang but was removed because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be judicial commissioner of Zhejiang but was removed because of an affair.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫王文韶薦其才，光緒十六年，召入都，除湖北按察使，署布政使。

translations.literal: Hunan governor Wang Wenshao recommended his ability; in Guangxu 16 he was summoned to the capital, appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei, and made acting provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan governor Wang Wenshao recommended his ability; in Guangxu 16 he was summoned to the capital, appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei, and made acting provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢直隸布政使，入對，時中東戰亟，見上形容憂悴，請日讀聖祖御纂周易，以期變不失常。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 20 he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili. When received in audience, with the Sino-Japanese war pressing and seeing the emperor’s worn and anxious appearance, he requested that the emperor read daily the Kangxi Emperor’s imperially compiled Zhouyi, hoping that amid change he would not lose constancy.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili. When received in audience, with the Sino-Japanese war pressing and seeing the emperor’s worn and anxious appearance, he requested that the emperor read daily the Kangxi Emperor’s imperially compiled Zhouyi, hoping that amid change he would not lose constancy.

sentences.zh: 他所陳奏語甚多，並稱旨。

translations.literal: His other memorial statements were numerous, and all pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His other memorials were many, and all met with the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 上以為忠，命治糈台，專摺奏事。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded him as loyal and ordered him to manage the grain depots and submit memorials on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him loyal and put him in charge of the grain depots with authority to submit memorials directly.

sentences.zh: 馬關和約成，泣曰：「殆不國矣！」

translations.literal: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was concluded, he wept and said: "The state is nearly lost!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed, he wept and said, "The dynasty is all but finished!"

sentences.zh: 明年，以榮祿薦，擢湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: The next year, on Ronglu's recommendation, he was promoted to Governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on Ronglu's recommendation, he was made Governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 撫幕有任驎者，植黨私利，至即重治之。

translations.literal: In the governor's secretariat there was Ren Lin, who formed a faction for private profit; as soon as Baozhen arrived he punished him severely.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Ren Lin in the governor's staff had built a clique for private gain; Baozhen punished him severely as soon as he took office.

sentences.zh: 直隸布政使王廉為關說，據以上聞，廉獲譴。

translations.literal: Zhili Provincial Treasurer Wang Lian interceded for him; Baozhen reported the facts to the throne, and Lian was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili treasurer Wang Lian pleaded on Ren's behalf; Baozhen reported the matter upward, and Wang was censured.

sentences.zh: 覆按史念祖被劾事，盡暴其任用非人狀，念祖遂褫職。

translations.literal: He reinvestigated the case in which Shi Nianzu had been impeached, fully exposing how Nianzu had employed unworthy men, and Nianzu was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed the impeachment of Shi Nianzu, fully exposing how Nianzu had appointed unfit men, and Nianzu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 繇是有伉直聲。

translations.literal: From this he gained a reputation for stern uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From this he gained a reputation for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 湘俗故闇僿，寶箴思以一隅致富強，為東南倡，先後設電信，置小輪，建製造槍彈廠，又立保衛局、南學會、時務學堂。

translations.literal: Hunan customs were formerly benighted and obstructed; Baozhen wished to make one corner rich and strong and be a leader for the southeast. In succession he set up telegraph lines, introduced steam launches, built a factory for manufacturing firearms and ammunition, and also established a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had long been backward and insular; Baozhen hoped to make the province a model of wealth and strength for the southeast. He set up telegraph lines, introduced steam launches, built an arms and ammunition factory, and founded a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.

sentences.zh: 延梁啟超主湘學，湘俗大變。

translations.literal: He invited Liang Qichao to direct Hunan learning, and local custom changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Liang Qichao to lead Hunan's schools, and local attitudes changed dramatically.

sentences.zh: 又疏請釐正學術及練兵、籌款諸大端，上皆嘉納，敕令持定見，毋為浮言動，並特旨褒勵之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting correction of scholarship and the major tasks of drilling troops and raising funds; the emperor approved all and ordered him to hold firm views and not be moved by loose talk, and also issued a special edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on reforming scholarship, drilling troops, and raising revenue; the emperor approved everything, told him to stand by his convictions and ignore loose talk, and issued a special edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 是時張之洞負盛名，司道咸屏息以伺。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and the provincial officials all held their breath and watched him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and the provincial officials all held their breath and watched him.

sentences.zh: 寶箴初綰鄂籓，遇事不合，獨與爭無私撓，之洞雖不懌，無如何也。

translations.literal: When Baozhen first took charge of Hubei’s provincial administration, whenever matters did not accord, he alone argued with Zhang without private compromise; though Zhidong was displeased, there was nothing he could do.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen first took charge of Hubei’s provincial administration, whenever matters did not accord, he alone argued with Zhang without private compromise; though Zhidong was displeased, there was nothing he could do.

sentences.zh: 久之，兩人深相結，凡條上新政皆聯銜，而鄂撫譚繼洵反不與。

translations.literal: In time the two became deeply allied; every memorial setting out new policies bore both their names, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun, by contrast, did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In time the two became deeply allied; every memorial setting out new policies bore both their names, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun, by contrast, did not participate.

sentences.zh: 會康有為言事數見效。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei’s policy proposals had repeatedly shown results.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kang Youwei’s policy proposals had repeatedly shown results.

sentences.zh: 寶箴素慕曾、胡薦士，因上言楊銳、劉光第、譚嗣同、林旭佐新政。

translations.literal: Baozhen had long admired how Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi recommended men, and therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen had long admired how Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi recommended men, and therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.

sentences.zh: 上方詔求通變才，遽擢京卿，參新政，於是四人上書論時事無顧忌。

translations.literal: The emperor had just issued an edict seeking men of adaptable talent; the four were abruptly promoted to grand secretaries in the capital to take part in the new policies, and thereafter they memorialized on current affairs without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just called for adaptable talent; the four were suddenly raised to high office in the capital to join the reforms, and from then on they spoke on public affairs without restraint.

sentences.zh: 寶箴又言四人雖才，恐資望輕，視事過易，原得厚重大臣如之洞者領之。

translations.literal: Baozhen also said that though the four were talented, he feared their standing was light and they would treat office too easily; he wished to have a weighty senior minister such as Zhidong lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen also said that though the four were able, their standing was slight and they might treat office too lightly; he asked that a senior figure such as Zhang Zhidong supervise them.

sentences.zh: 疏上而太后已出訓政，誅四京卿，罪及舉主，寶箴去官，其子主事三立亦革職，並毀湘學所著學約、界說、劄記、答問諸書。

translations.literal: By the time the memorial arrived, the Empress Dowager had already issued instructions and resumed government; the four capital officials were executed, blame extended to their recommender, Baozhen left office, his son Sanli, a ministry secretary, was also dismissed, and the Hunan school's works Xueyue, Jieshuo, Zhaji, and Dawen were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the memorial arrived the empress dowager had resumed power; the four capital officials were executed, blame fell on their recommender, Baozhen was dismissed, his son Sanli was stripped of office, and the Hunan school's Xueyue, Jieshuo, Zhaji, and Dawen were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 初，寧鄉已革道員周漢，以張揭帖攻西教為總督所治。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou Han, a dismissed intendant from Ningxiang, had been punished by the governor-general for posting placards attacking the Western religion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the dismissed intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor-general for posting anti-Christian placards.

sentences.zh: 寶箴至，漢復刊帖傳布，寶箴令毀之，漢毆毀帖者，寶箴怒，下之獄。

translations.literal: When Baozhen arrived, Han again printed placards and circulated them. Baozhen ordered them destroyed; Han beat those who destroyed the placards, and Baozhen angrily had him jailed.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen arrived, Zhou Han printed placards again; Baozhen ordered them destroyed, Zhou Han beat those who tore them down, and Baozhen had him jailed in anger.

sentences.zh: 舊黨恨次骨，然喜新之士，亦以此翕然稱之。

translations.literal: The old faction hated him to the marrow, yet men who favored the new learning also united in praising him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The conservative faction hated him bitterly, yet reform-minded men united in praise for the same act.

sentences.zh: 既去，諸所營構便於民者，雖效益已著，皆廢毀無一存雲。

translations.literal: After he left, all the institutions he had built for the people's benefit, though their good effects were already evident, were abolished and destroyed until not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, every institution he had built for the people, though already proving useful, was abolished until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 黃遵憲，字公度，嘉應州人。

translations.literal: Huang Zunxian, courtesy name Gongdu, was a native of Jiaying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zunxian, whose courtesy name was Gongdu, came from Jiaying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為道員。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he bought appointment as a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 充使日參贊，著日本國誌上之朝。

translations.literal: He served as counsellor on the mission to Japan and submitted his Riben guozhi to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attaché on the mission to Japan and submitted his Record of Japan to the court.

sentences.zh: 旋移舊金山總領事。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to be consul-general at San Francisco.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made consul-general at San Francisco.

sentences.zh: 美吏嘗藉口衛生，逮華僑滿獄。

translations.literal: American officials once used sanitation as a pretext to arrest Chinese residents until the prisons were full.
translations.idiomatic: American officials once used public health as a pretext to arrest Chinese residents until the prisons were packed.

sentences.zh: 徑詣獄中，令從者度其容積，曰：「此處衛生顧右於僑居邪？」

translations.literal: Zunxian went straight to the prison and ordered his attendants to measure its capacity, saying: "Is sanitation here really better cared for than in the Chinese quarter?"
translations.idiomatic: Zunxian went straight to the jail and had his attendants measure its space, saying, "Is sanitation really better here than where the Chinese live?"

sentences.zh: 吏謝，遽釋之。

translations.literal: The American officials apologized and released them at once.
translations.idiomatic: The officials apologized and released them immediately.

sentences.zh: 歷湖南長寶鹽法道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He served as salt controller of Hunan's Changbao Circuit and acted as judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as salt controller of Hunan's Changbao Circuit and acted as judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時寶箴為巡撫，行新政，遵憲首倡民治於眾曰：「亦自治其身，自治其鄉而已。

translations.literal: Baozhen was then governor and carrying out new policies; Zunxian first advocated people's self-government before the public, saying: "It means governing yourself and governing your own township.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baozhen was then governor and pursuing reforms; Zunxian first preached popular self-government to the people, saying: "It means governing yourself and governing your own township.

sentences.zh: 由一鄉推之一縣、一府、一省，以迄全國，可以成共和之郅治，臻大同之盛軌。」

translations.literal: From one township extend it to one county, one prefecture, one province, and then to the whole country, and one may attain the highest government of a republic and reach the great path of universal harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Extend that from one township to a county, a prefecture, a province, and then the whole country, and you can reach the ideal of republican government and the great harmony of the Datong age."

sentences.zh: 於是略仿西國巡警之制，設保衛局，凡與民利民瘼相麗，而為一方民力能舉者，悉屬之，領以民望，而官輔其不及焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon, roughly imitating the Western police patrol system, he established the Public Security Bureau; all matters touching the people's benefit and hardship that the local people had strength to undertake were placed under it, led by men of local standing, while officials assisted where they fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He then roughly copied the Western police system and set up a Public Security Bureau; everything touching local welfare that the people could manage was placed under respected local leaders, with officials helping where needed.

sentences.zh: 尋解職，奉出使日本之命，未行而黨禍起，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon he left office and received orders to go as envoy to Japan, but before he departed the factional disaster broke out and he returned home dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office and was ordered to Japan as envoy, but before he could depart the reform purge began and he went home.

sentences.zh: 著有人境廬詩草等。

translations.literal: His writings include Renjinglu Shicao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote works including Renjinglu Shicao and others.

sentences.zh: 曾鉌，字懷清，喜塔臘氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Zeng He, courtesy name Huaiqing, of the Hitara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng He, whose courtesy name was Huaiqing, of the Hitara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父慶昀，寧夏將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qingyun was General of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingyun was General of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 以任子為工部主事，累遷郎中，充軍機章京，轉御史。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Works, was promoted in succession to bureau director, served as a clerk in the Grand Council, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Works as a director, rose to bureau director, served on the Grand Council staff, and became a censor.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，出為陝西督糧道。

translations.literal: In Guangxu year nine, he was sent out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 he was sent out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 西、同各屬農民納糧例繳省倉，道塗艱遠，多弊竇，設法清釐之，民稱便。

translations.literal: In Xi'an, Tongzhou, and their subordinate districts, peasants normally paid grain tax to the provincial granary; the routes were long and difficult and there were many abuses. He devised methods to clarify and regulate it, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xi'an and Tongzhou circuits peasants normally paid grain tax to the provincial granary; the routes were long and corrupt. He reformed the system, and the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 三輔士風樸僿，藝事苦窳，延長安柏景偉、咸陽劉光蕡主關中書院，督課實學，士論翕然。

translations.literal: The scholarly culture of the Sanfu region was plain and narrow, and literary work was poor; he invited Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangfen of Xianyang to head the Guanzhong Academy, supervised instruction in practical learning, and scholarly opinion rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship in the Sanfu region was plain and narrow, and literary work was poor; he brought Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangfen of Xianyang to head the Guanzhong Academy, stressed practical studies, and scholars rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 又設蠶桑局，聘織師教以煮湅織染法，歲出絲帛埒齊、豫。

translations.literal: He also established a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach boiling, reeling, weaving, and dyeing methods, and each year produced silk and cloth rivaling Qi and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up a sericulture bureau, hired weavers to teach reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year produced silk output rivaling Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，母憂解職。

translations.literal: The next year, on his mother's death, he left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起故官，俄遷甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to his former office and was soon promoted to Provincial Treasurer of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned to office and was soon made Treasurer of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，調直隸，迴避，留本任。

translations.literal: In year twenty-four, he was transferred to Zhili, but because of the avoidance rule he remained in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four he was transferred to Zhili but stayed in Gansu on account of the avoidance rule.

sentences.zh: 擢湖北巡撫，慨然曰：「時艱至此，猶可拘成法不變耶？」

translations.literal: He was promoted to Governor of Hubei and said with feeling: "Times are this difficult; can we still be bound by fixed rules and not change?"
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Hubei and said with feeling, "Times are this desperate; can we still cling to old rules and refuse to change?"

sentences.zh: 於是假陝甘總督印上陳補官、掣籤、度支、訟獄四事，宜變通成例，厚植國本。

translations.literal: He then used the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general's seal to memorialize on four matters--filling offices, drawing lots for posts, revenue, and litigation--saying that precedents should be adapted to strengthen the foundations of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He then used the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general's seal to memorialize on filling offices, drawing lots for posts, revenue, and litigation, urging flexible change to strengthen the state.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士貽穀、光祿寺少卿張仲炘彈其亂政，詔褫職。

translations.literal: Reader-in-waiting Yigu and Guanglu Temple Vice Minister Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for disordering government, and an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-waiting Yigu and Guanglu Temple Vice Minister Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for subverting government, and he was dismissed by edict.

sentences.zh: 始，曾鉌官京朝，家綦貧，僦居陋室。

translations.literal: At first, when Zeng He served in capital offices, his family was extremely poor and rented a humble room.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng He first served in Beijing his family was very poor and he lived in rented quarters.

sentences.zh: 及任外台，孜孜民事，不顧問有無。

translations.literal: When he came to hold a provincial appointment, he worked diligently at the people's affairs, without regard to whether he himself had enough or not.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held office in the provinces, he devoted himself tirelessly to the people's affairs, heedless of his own comfort.

sentences.zh: 既閒廢，出入皆徒步，民恆歲醵金濟之。

translations.literal: After he was dismissed and idle, he went in and out everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly pooled money each year to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he went everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly collected money each year to support him.

sentences.zh: 後益困，至敝衣鬻卜都市。

translations.literal: Later his straits grew worse, until he wore tattered clothes and sold divination in the capital markets.
translations.idiomatic: His circumstances worsened until he wore threadbare clothes and sold divination in the city markets.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，總督端方為奏復原官。

translations.literal: When Xuantong became the reign title, Governor-General Duanfang memorialized to restore his original office.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Governor-General Duanfang memorialized to restore his former rank.

sentences.zh: 楊深秀，字儀村，本名毓秀，山西聞喜人。

translations.literal: Yang Shenxiu, courtesy name Yicun, originally named Yuxiu, was a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shenxiu, whose courtesy name was Yicun and whose original name was Yuxiu, came from Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 少穎敏，諳中西算術。

translations.literal: As a youth he was sharp and quick-witted and thoroughly versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was sharp and quick-witted, and thoroughly versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.

sentences.zh: 同治初，以舉人入貲為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi, as a provincial graduate he bought appointment as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, as a provincial graduate he bought appointment as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 假歸，值晉大饑，閻敬銘銜命籌賑，深秀條上改革差徭法，困少蘇。

translations.literal: While on leave he returned home and encountered the great famine in Shanxi; Yan Jingming had been ordered to plan relief, and Shenxiu submitted a detailed plan to reform corvée and labor levies, so the people in distress somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: While on leave he encountered the great famine in Shanxi; Yan Jingming, charged with organizing relief, received Shenxiu's detailed plan to reform corvée and labor levies, and the people's distress was somewhat relieved.

sentences.zh: 十五年，成進士，就本官遷郎中，轉御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred in his original post to department director, and then to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he took his jinshi degree, was promoted within his existing office to department director, and then transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「時勢危迫，不革舊無以圖新，不變法無以圖存。」

translations.literal: He once said: "The times are perilously urgent; without reforming the old there is no means to plan the new, and without changing the laws there is no means to plan survival."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The times are perilously urgent: without overturning the old there is no way to plan the new, and without changing the laws there is no way to plan for survival."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，俄人脅割旅順、大連灣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Russians coerced the cession of Lüshun and Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Russia coerced China into ceding Lüshun and Dalian Bay.

sentences.zh: 深秀力請聯英、日拒之，詞甚切直。

translations.literal: Shenxiu urgently petitioned to ally with Britain and Japan in resisting them, his language very forceful and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu urgently petitioned that China ally with Britain and Japan to resist, in language that was forceful and blunt.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷銳意行新政，而大臣恆多異議。

translations.literal: At the time the court was keen to carry out new policies, but senior ministers often had many objections.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then eager to enact new policies, but senior ministers constantly raised objections.

sentences.zh: 深秀乃與徐致靖先後疏請定國是，又以取士之法未善，請參酌宋、元、明舊制，釐正文體，下其議於禮部，尚書許應騤心非之，未奏也。

translations.literal: Shenxiu and Xu Zhijing then submitted successive memorials requesting that the national course be fixed. He also found the method of selecting talent inadequate and asked that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted, that literary forms be standardized, and that the matter be referred to the Ministry of Rites. Minister Xu Yingkui privately disapproved and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu and Xu Zhijing then submitted successive memorials asking that the national course be fixed; finding the method of selecting talent inadequate, Shenxiu urged that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted, literary forms standardized, and the matter referred to the Ministry of Rites, but Minister Xu Yingkui privately disapproved and never forwarded the proposal.

sentences.zh: 會議經濟特科務減額，於是深秀合宋伯魯彈其阻撓。

translations.literal: When the economic special examination was discussed and efforts were made to reduce its quota, Shenxiu joined Song Bolu in impeaching him for obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: When the economic special examination came up for discussion with efforts to cut its quota, Shenxiu joined Song Bolu in impeaching Xu Yingkui for obstruction.

sentences.zh: 上令應騤自陳，奏上，劾康有為夤緣要津，請罷斥，詞連深秀，上不之詰也。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yingkui to explain himself. In the submitted memorial, he impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed; the wording implicated Shenxiu, but the Emperor did not pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Xu Yingkui to explain himself; in his reply Xu impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed, implicating Shenxiu in the wording, but the Emperor did not pursue Shenxiu.

sentences.zh: 御史文悌劾深秀傳布有為所立保國會，並暴有為交通內外狀，德宗責以代人報復，反獲咎。

translations.literal: Censor Wenti impeached Shenxiu for disseminating the Baoguo Society founded by Youwei and also exposed Youwei's dealings inside and outside the court. Dezong rebuked him for retaliating on another's behalf, and he instead incurred blame.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wenti impeached Shenxiu for disseminating the Baoguo Society founded by Kang Youwei and exposed Youwei's dealings inside and outside the court; Emperor Dezong rebuked Wenti for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wenti himself was punished.

sentences.zh: 深秀益感奮，連上書請設譯書局，派王公遊歷各國，並定遊學日本章程，皆報可。

translations.literal: Shenxiu was all the more stirred to action, and in successive memorials requested the establishment of a Translation Bureau, the dispatch of princes and dukes to tour the various countries, and the fixing of regulations for study in Japan; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu was all the more stirred to action, and in a series of memorials asked that a Translation Bureau be established, that princes and nobles be sent to tour foreign countries, and that regulations for study in Japan be drawn up; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 又請試庶官，日番二十人，料簡貞實，而汰其庸愚罷老不諳時務者，繇是廷臣益側目。

translations.literal: He also asked to test ordinary officials, twenty per day in rotation, to select the upright and sincere and eliminate the mediocre, foolish, worn out, and aged who did not understand current affairs; from this court ministers looked upon him with ever greater resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed testing ordinary officials twenty at a time each day, selecting the upright and sincere while weeding out the mediocre, foolish, and aged who did not understand current affairs; from this the court ministers looked upon him with growing hostility.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫陳寶箴圖治甚急，中蜚語，深秀為剖辨之，上以特旨褒寶箴，寶箴乃得行其志。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Chen Baozhen pressed urgently for reform but was struck by slanderous talk; Shenxiu analyzed and defended him, and the Emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, so Baozhen was able to carry out his plans.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Governor Chen Baozhen was pressing hard for reform when slander spread against him; Shenxiu defended him in a memorial, and the Emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, who was then able to carry out his plans.

sentences.zh: 八月，政變，舉朝惴惴，懼大誅至，獨深秀抗疏請太后歸政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the coup occurred; the whole court trembled, fearing a great purge would come, but Shenxiu alone submitted a forceful memorial asking the Empress Dowager to return government to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the coup occurred; the whole court trembled, fearing mass executions, yet Shenxiu alone submitted a bold memorial asking the Empress Dowager to restore power to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 方疏未上時，其子黻田苦口諫止，深秀厲聲叱之退。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was submitted, his son Futian pleaded earnestly to stop him, but Shenxiu sharply rebuked him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial could be submitted, his son Futian pleaded desperately with him to desist; Shenxiu sharply rebuked him and ordered him away.

sentences.zh: 俄被逮，論棄市。

translations.literal: Soon he was arrested and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was arrested and condemned to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 深秀性鯁直，嘗面折人過，以此叢忌。

translations.literal: Shenxiu was blunt and upright by nature and often corrected people's faults to their faces, thereby accumulating resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxiu was blunt and upright by nature, often rebuking others to their faces over their faults, and for this he accumulated many enemies.

sentences.zh: 官臺諫十閱月，封事二十餘上，稿不具存，惟獄中詩三章流傳於世。

translations.literal: In ten months as a remonstrance official on the censorate, he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts are not fully preserved—only three poems from prison circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In ten months on the censorate he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts are not fully preserved—only three poems written in prison survive.

sentences.zh: 著有虛聲堂稿、聞喜縣新志。

translations.literal: His works include Xushengtang gao and Wenxi xian xinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Xushengtang gao and Wenxi xian xinzhi.

sentences.zh: 楊銳，字叔嶠，四川綿竹人。

translations.literal: Yang Rui, courtesy name Shuqiao, was a native of Mianzhu, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui, whose courtesy name was Shuqiao, came from Mianzhu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 少俊慧，督學張之洞奇其才，招入幕。

translations.literal: In youth he was handsome and clever; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong marveled at his talent and recruited him into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brilliant and quick-witted; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong was struck by his talent and brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 肄業尊經書院，年最少，嘗冠其曹。

translations.literal: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though the youngest in years, he often led his class.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though the youngest in his cohort, he often ranked first among his peers.

sentences.zh: 優貢朝考得知縣。

translations.literal: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the metropolitan tribute examination and was appointed district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as an outstanding tribute student, he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 之洞督兩廣，從赴粵。

translations.literal: When Zhidong became governor-general of the Two Guang, Yang Rui accompanied him to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhidong became governor-general of the Two Guang, Yang Rui accompanied him to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 光緒十一年，舉順天鄉試，考取內閣中書。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 11 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 11 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，之洞薦應經濟特科。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 24, Zhidong recommended him for the special economics examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24, Zhidong recommended him for the special economics examination.

sentences.zh: 又以陳寶箴薦，與劉光第、譚嗣同、林旭並加四品卿，充軍機章京，參新政。

translations.literal: Again through Chen Baozhen’s recommendation, he, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu, was given fourth-rank ministerial title, appointed a Grand Council secretary, and took part in the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: Again through Chen Baozhen’s recommendation, he, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu, was given fourth-rank ministerial title, appointed a Grand Council secretary, and took part in the new policies.

sentences.zh: 召見，銳面陳興學、練兵為救亡策，稱旨。

translations.literal: When summoned for audience, Rui stated directly that promoting education and drilling troops were strategies for saving the nation, and this pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for audience, Rui stated directly that promoting education and drilling troops were strategies for saving the nation, and this pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 七月，禮部主事王照上封事，尚書許應騤等格不奏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Ministry of Rites secretary Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Ministry of Rites secretary Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not present it.

sentences.zh: 上聞，震怒，盡褫尚書侍郎六人革職，朝臣皆不自安。

translations.literal: When the Emperor learned of it, he was furious and stripped all six ministers and vice ministers of their posts; court officials were all ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of this he was furious and dismissed all six ministers and vice ministers; the court was thrown into unease.

sentences.zh: 上手詔密諭云：「近日朕仰觀聖母意旨，不欲退此老耄昏庸大臣而進英勇通達之人，亦不欲將法盡變。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally issued a secret hand-edict to Rui, saying: "Recently I have looked up to observe the Empress Dowager's intent: she does not wish to remove these aged, senile, and incompetent ministers and advance brave and penetrating men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally sent Rui a secret hand-edict: "Of late I have observed the Empress Dowager's intent—she does not wish to remove these aged and incompetent ministers in favor of bold and capable men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely.

sentences.zh: 朕豈不知積弱不振，非力行新政不可？

translations.literal: Do I not know that China has long been weak and failing, and that vigorous new policies are indispensable?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that China has long been weak and enfeebled, and that only vigorous new policies can save it?

sentences.zh: 然此時不惟朕權力所不及，若強行之，朕位且不能保。

translations.literal: Yet at this time not only is my power insufficient; if I force matters, I cannot even keep my throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this moment my power does not reach that far; if I force the matter, I cannot even keep my throne.

sentences.zh: 爾與劉光弟、譚嗣同、林旭等詳悉籌議，必如何而後能進用英達，使新政及時舉行，又不致少拂聖意，即具奏，候朕審擇，不勝焦慮之至！」

translations.literal: You, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others, must deliberate carefully on how able men can be advanced so the new policies may be carried out in time without even slightly offending Her Majesty's wishes; submit a memorial at once for my review. My anxiety is beyond measure!"
translations.idiomatic: You, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others, must deliberate carefully on how to advance able men so that the new policies may proceed in good time without the least offense to the Empress Dowager's wishes. Memorialize at once for my review. My anxiety is beyond words!"

sentences.zh: 銳復奏言：「太后親挈大位授之皇上，皇上宜以孝先天下，遇事將順。

translations.literal: Rui again memorialized: "The Empress Dowager personally took the great position and gave it to Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all under Heaven and accommodate her in every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Rui memorialized in reply: "The Empress Dowager personally invested the throne in Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all else and accommodate her wishes in every matter.

sentences.zh: 變法宜有次第，進退大臣不宜太驟。」

translations.literal: Reform should proceed in due order; advancing and dismissing ministers should not be too abrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Reform should proceed step by step; the advancement and dismissal of ministers should not be too sudden."

sentences.zh: 上是之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 已而太后再訓政，諸言新政者皆予重誅。

translations.literal: Before long the Empress Dowager again assumed regency; all who spoke for the new policies were given severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Empress Dowager resumed regency, and all who had advocated the new policies were severely punished.

sentences.zh: 銳既下獄，自揣實無罪，謂即訊不難白，次日，遽詔與光第等同棄市。

translations.literal: Once Rui had been imprisoned, he judged himself truly innocent and thought that if interrogated he could easily make it clear. The next day, however, an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Guangdi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Once imprisoned, Rui believed himself innocent and thought he could easily clear his name under interrogation, but the next day an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Guangdi and the others.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，銳子慶昶繳手詔於都察院，請代奏，始傳於世。

translations.literal: When Xuantong became the reign title, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the hand-edict to the Censorate and requested that it memorialize on his behalf; only then did it circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the hand-edict to the Censorate and asked that it be forwarded to the throne; only then did it become known to the world.

sentences.zh: 劉光第，字裴村，四川富順人。

translations.literal: Liu Guangdi, courtesy name Peicun, was a native of Fushun in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangdi, whose courtesy name was Peicun, came from Fushun in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In Guangxu year nine he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed ministry secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 9 he took his jinshi degree and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 治事精嚴，因讞獄忤長官​​，遂退而閉戶勤學，絕跡不詣署。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was meticulous and strict; because of a criminal case he offended his superior, whereupon he withdrew, closed his doors, and studied diligently, cutting off all visits to the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He handled business with exacting rigor; when a criminal case brought him into conflict with his superior, he withdrew, shut his doors to study, and stopped going to the office altogether.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，而性廉介，非舊交，雖禮饋弗受。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor, yet his nature was upright and incorruptible; unless they were old friends, he would not accept gifts even of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor, but he was incorruptible by nature and would accept no courtesy gift from anyone who was not an old friend.

sentences.zh: 獨與楊銳善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Yang Rui alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui alone numbered among his close friends.

sentences.zh: 通周官、禮及大小戴禮記。

translations.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Record of Rites of the Elder and Younger Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and both recensions of the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其應召也，亦以陳寶箴薦，然非其素志，將具疏辭，川人官京朝者力勸之。

translations.literal: When he answered the summons, it was also on Chen Baozhen's recommendation; yet this was not his original intent, and he was about to prepare a memorial declining, but Sichuan officials serving in the capital strongly urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the summons on Chen Baozhen's recommendation too, though it was not what he had wanted; he was preparing a memorial to decline when Sichuan colleagues in the capital pressed him hard to accept.

sentences.zh: 一日，召見，力陳時危民困，外患日迫，亟宜虛懷圖治，上稱善。

translations.literal: One day he was summoned for audience and forcefully stated that the times were perilous, the people distressed, and foreign danger pressing daily; the throne should urgently open its mind and plan good government—the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: One day he was received in audience and spoke urgently of national peril, popular distress, and the daily tightening of foreign pressure, urging the emperor to govern with an open mind; the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 惟時言路宏啟，臣民奏事日數百計，竟日批答，簽識可否，以待上裁。

translations.literal: At that time the channels of remonstrance were broadly opened; memorials from officials and commoners numbered hundreds each day; Guangdi spent the whole day drafting responses, marking approval or rejection, awaiting the emperor's final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial channels were then wide open, with hundreds of submissions arriving daily; Guangdi spent entire days drafting replies and marking what should stand or fall, all for the emperor's final ruling.

sentences.zh: 退語所親曰：「吾終不任此，行當亟假歸矣！」

translations.literal: Afterward he told those close to him, “I cannot bear this responsibility to the end; I mean to ask leave and go home at once!”
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told those close to him, “I cannot bear this responsibility to the end; I mean to ask leave and go home at once!”

sentences.zh: 未一月而禍作，光第自投獄。

translations.literal: Less than a month later disaster broke out, and Guangdi surrendered himself to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later the disaster broke out, and Guangdi surrendered himself to prison.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，協辦大學士剛毅監斬，光第詫曰：「未訊而誅，何哉？」

translations.literal: At the execution, Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading, and Guangdi cried out in astonishment: "To execute a man without trial--why?"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution, Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading, and Guangdi cried out in astonishment, "To execute a man without trial--why?"

sentences.zh: 令跪聽旨，光第不可，曰：「祖制，雖盜賊，臨刑呼冤，當復訊。

translations.literal: He was ordered to kneel and hear the edict, but Guangdi refused, saying: "By ancestral law, even a thief who cries injustice at execution must be interrogated again.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to kneel and hear the edict; Guangdi refused, saying, "By ancestral law, even a thief who cries injustice at execution must be interrogated again.

sentences.zh: 吾輩縱不足惜，如國體何！」

translations.literal: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!”
translations.idiomatic: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!”

sentences.zh: 剛毅默不應，再詢之，曰：「吾奉命監刑耳，他何知？」

translations.literal: Gangyi was silent and did not answer. When questioned again, he said: "I am only here under orders to supervise the execution; what else would I know?"
translations.idiomatic: Gangyi was silent and did not answer. When questioned again, he replied, "I am only here under orders to supervise the execution; what else would I know?"

sentences.zh: 獄卒強之跪，光第崛立自如。

translations.literal: The jailers tried to force him to kneel, but Guangdi stood upright and unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: The jailers tried to force him to his knees, but Guangdi stood straight and unmoved.

sentences.zh: 楊銳呼曰：「裴村，跪！

translations.literal: Yang Rui called out: "Peicun, kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rui called out, "Peicun, kneel!

sentences.zh: 跪！

translations.literal: Kneel!
translations.idiomatic: Kneel!

sentences.zh: 遵旨而已。」

translations.literal: It is only to obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: It is only to obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 乃跪就戮。

translations.literal: Then he knelt and submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Then he knelt and went to his death.

sentences.zh: 著有介白堂詩文集。

translations.literal: His writings include Jiebaitang shiwenji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Jiebaitang shiwenji.

sentences.zh: 譚嗣同，字復生，湖南瀏陽人。

translations.literal: Tan Sitong, courtesy name Fusheng, was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Sitong, whose courtesy name was Fusheng, came from Liuyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父繼洵，湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Jixun was Governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan Jixun was Governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，文為奇肆。

translations.literal: From youth he was free-spirited and had great ambition; his writing was bold and unconventional.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was spirited and ambitious, and his prose was bold and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 其學以日新為主，視倫常舊說若無足措意者。

translations.literal: His learning took daily renewal as its principle; he regarded conventional morality and old doctrines as scarcely worth a thought.
translations.idiomatic: He took daily renewal as the heart of his learning and treated conventional morality and inherited doctrine as hardly worth notice.

sentences.zh: 繼洵素謹飭，以是頗見惡。

translations.literal: Jixun was stern and proper by nature, and for this Sitong was much disliked by him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was stern and proper by nature, and for this Sitong was much disliked by him.

sentences.zh: 嗣同乃遊新疆劉錦棠幕，以同知入貲為知府，銓江蘇。

translations.literal: Sitong then served on Liu Jintang’s staff in Xinjiang, purchased appointment as a prefect through the rank of subprefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong then served on Liu Jintang’s staff in Xinjiang, purchased appointment as a prefect through the rank of subprefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 陳寶箴撫湖南，嗣同還鄉佐新政。

translations.literal: When Chen Baozhen governed Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baozhen governed Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.

sentences.zh: 梁啟超倡辦南學會，嗣同為之長。

translations.literal: Liang Qichao initiated the Southern Study Society, and Sitong served as its head.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qichao initiated the Southern Study Society, and Sitong served as its head.

sentences.zh: 屆會期，集者恆數百人，聞嗣同慷慨論時事，多感動。

translations.literal: At meeting times, several hundred people regularly gathered, and many were moved when they heard Sitong speak passionately about current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At meeting times, several hundred people regularly gathered, and many were moved when they heard Sitong speak passionately about current affairs.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，召入都，奏對稱旨，擢四品卿、軍機章京。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 24 he was summoned to the capital; his audience replies pleased the throne, and he was promoted to fourth-rank ministerial title and Grand Council secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24 he was summoned to the capital; his audience replies pleased the throne, and he was promoted to fourth-rank ministerial title and Grand Council secretary.

sentences.zh: 四人雖同被命，每召對，嗣同建議獨多。

translations.literal: Although the four men received the same appointment, at each audience Sitong alone offered especially many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Although the four men received the same appointment, at each audience Sitong alone offered especially many proposals.

sentences.zh: 上欲開懋勤殿，設顧問官，令嗣同擬旨，必載明前朝故事，將親詣頤和園請命太后。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to open Maoqin Hall and establish advisory officials; he ordered Sitong to draft the edict, requiring it to set out former-dynasty precedents clearly, and planned personally to go to the Summer Palace to request the empress dowager’s approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to open Maoqin Hall and establish advisory officials; he ordered Sitong to draft the edict, requiring it to set out former-dynasty precedents clearly, and planned personally to go to the Summer Palace to request the empress dowager’s approval.

sentences.zh: 嗣同退謂人曰：「今乃知上絕無權也！」

translations.literal: Sitong withdrew and told others, “Now I know the emperor has absolutely no power!”
translations.idiomatic: Sitong withdrew and told others, “Now I know the emperor has absolutely no power!”

sentences.zh: 時榮祿督畿輔，袁世凱以監司練兵天津。

translations.literal: At the time Ronglu governed the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai, as a surveillance commissioner, trained troops at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ronglu governed the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai, as a surveillance commissioner, trained troops at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 詔擢世凱侍郎，召入覲。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Shikai to vice minister and summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Shikai to vice minister and summoned him for audience.

sentences.zh: 嗣同嘗夜詣世凱有所議。

translations.literal: Sitong once went at night to Shikai to discuss something.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong once went at night to Shikai to discuss something.

sentences.zh: 明日，世凱返天津。

translations.literal: The next day Shikai returned to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shikai returned to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 越晨，太后自頤和園還宮，收政權。

translations.literal: The following morning, the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the palace and took back political power.
translations.idiomatic: The following morning, the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the palace and took back political power.

sentences.zh: 啟超避匿日本使館，嗣同往見之，勸嗣同東遊。

translations.literal: Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation. Sitong went to see him, and Qichao urged Sitong to travel east.
translations.idiomatic: Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation. Sitong went to see him, and Qichao urged Sitong to travel east.

sentences.zh: 嗣同曰：「不有行者，無以圖將來；

translations.literal: Sitong said, “Without someone who goes on living, there is no way to plan for the future;
translations.idiomatic: Sitong said, “Without someone who goes on living, there is no way to plan for the future;

sentences.zh: 不有死者，無以酬聖主。」

translations.literal: without one who dies, there is no way to repay the sagely sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: without someone who dies, there is no way to repay a devoted sovereign."

sentences.zh: 卒不去。

translations.literal: In the end he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斬於市。

translations.literal: Before long he was beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 著有仁學及莽蒼蒼齋詩集等。

translations.literal: He wrote Renxue and Mangcangcangzhai shiji, among other works.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Renxue and Mangcangcangzhai shiji, among other works.

sentences.zh: 唐才常，字佛塵。

translations.literal: Tang Caichang, courtesy name Fochen.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Caichang, courtesy name Fochen.

sentences.zh: 少與嗣同齊名，稱「瀏陽二生」，兩湖學堂高材生也。

translations.literal: From youth he was equally famous with Sitong, and they were called “the Two Students of Liuyang”; he was an outstanding student of the Lianghu Academy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was equally famous with Sitong, and they were called “the Two Students of Liuyang”; he was an outstanding student of the Lianghu Academy.

sentences.zh: 聞嗣同死，憂憤，屢有所謀，每言及德宗，常泣下。

translations.literal: Hearing of Sitong’s death, he was grieved and indignant and repeatedly made plans; whenever he spoke of Emperor Dezong, he would often weep.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Sitong’s death, he was grieved and indignant and repeatedly made plans; whenever he spoke of Emperor Dezong, he would often weep.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮出狩，才常陰結富有會謀舉事，號勤王，將攻武、漢。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 26, when the two palaces went out on progress, Caichang secretly organized the Fuyou Society and planned to rise, calling it loyal rescue of the throne, intending to attack Wuchang and Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26, when the two palaces went out on progress, Caichang secretly organized the Fuyou Society and planned to rise, calling it loyal rescue of the throne, intending to attack Wuchang and Hankou.

sentences.zh: 被獲，慷慨言無所隱，請就死，遂殺之。

translations.literal: He was captured; speaking boldly he concealed nothing, asked to die, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Captured, he spoke without concealment and asked only to die; he was killed.

sentences.zh: 林旭，字暾谷，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Lin Xu, courtesy name Tangu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xu, whose courtesy name was Tangu, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉本省鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At nineteen he placed first in the provincial examination of his province.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he topped the provincial examinations in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 後試禮部，值構釁，糾同試者上書論時事，不報。

translations.literal: Later he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination; when the Sino-Japanese conflict broke out, he joined fellow candidates in memorializing on current affairs, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He later took the metropolitan examination; when war broke out with Japan, he joined fellow candidates in a memorial on public affairs, but the court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He bought appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時康有為倡言變法，先於京師立粵學會，以振厲士氣，而蜀學、浙學、陝學、閩學諸會繼之。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Youwei advocated reform; he first established the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to rouse scholarly morale, and the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian study societies followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Youwei began calling for reform, he first founded the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to stir scholarly morale; the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian societies followed.

sentences.zh: 旭為閩學會領袖，又充保國會會員。

translations.literal: Xu was leader of the Fujian Study Society and also served as a member of the Society for the Preservation of the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu led the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Baoguo Society.

sentences.zh: 榮祿先為福州將軍，雅好閩士，及至天津，延旭入幕。

translations.literal: Ronglu had earlier been General of Fuzhou and had long favored Fujian scholars; when he reached Tianjin he took Xu into his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Ronglu, formerly General of Fuzhou, had long favored Fujian scholars; when he went to Tianjin he brought Xu onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 俄以奏保人才召見，操土語，上不盡解。

translations.literal: Soon, on memorial recommendation as talent, Xu was summoned for audience; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor did not fully understand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned on memorial recommendation; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor could not fully follow him.

sentences.zh: 退繕摺，上稱善，遂命與譚嗣同等同參機務，詔諭多旭起草。

translations.literal: He withdrew and drafted a memorial; the Emperor praised it, then ordered him to join Tan Sitong and the others in participating in confidential affairs, and many edicts were drafted by Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He then revised his memorial, which the Emperor praised, and was ordered to join Tan Sitong and the others in confidential duties; many edicts were drafted by Xu.

sentences.zh: 及變起，同戮於市，年二十有四。

translations.literal: When the coup broke out he was executed in the marketplace together with the others, at the age of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup came he was executed in the marketplace with the others, aged twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 著有晚翠軒詩集。

translations.literal: His writings include Wancuixuan shiji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Wancuixuan shiji.

sentences.zh: 妻沈葆楨孫女，聞變，仰藥不死，以毀卒。

translations.literal: His wife was a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen; when she heard of the disaster she took poison but did not die, and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Shen Baozhen's granddaughter; on hearing the news she took poison but survived, and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 康廣仁，名有溥，以字行，有為弟。

translations.literal: Kang Guangren, personal name Youpu, styled by his courtesy name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guangren, whose personal name was Youpu and who went by his courtesy name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少從兄學。

translations.literal: From youth he studied under his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied under his brother.

sentences.zh: 有為上書請改革，廣仁謂當先變科舉，庶人才可出。

translations.literal: When Youwei memorialized requesting reform, Guangren said that the examinations should be changed first, so that talent might emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When Youwei memorialized for reform, Guangren urged that the examinations be changed first so talent could emerge.

sentences.zh: 其後罷鄉會試、製藝，而歲科試未變，廣仁激勵言官抗疏論之，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: After the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the eight-legged essay were abolished, the annual and triennial examinations had not yet changed. Guangren stirred the censors to submit forceful memorials on the matter, and obtained an approving edict.
translations.idiomatic: After the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the eight-legged essay were abolished, the annual local tests remained unchanged; Guangren pressed censors to memorialize boldly, and the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 於是廣仁語有為：「今科舉既廢，宜且南歸興學專教育，俟養成多數有用才，數年後乃可云改革也。」

translations.literal: Guangren then told Youwei: "Now that the examinations have been abolished, you should for the moment return south, promote schools, and devote yourself to education. Wait until a large number of useful talents have been trained; only after several years can reform be spoken of."
translations.idiomatic: Guangren then told Youwei, "With the examinations gone, you should go south and devote yourself to education, train many useful men, and only after several years speak of reform again."

sentences.zh: 有為不忍去。

translations.literal: Youwei could not bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei could not bring himself to leave.

sentences.zh: 及初聞變，廣仁復趣有為歸。

translations.literal: When he first heard of the coup, Guangren again urged Youwei to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the coup first came, Guangren again urged Youwei to flee.

sentences.zh: 有為走，廣仁被逮。

translations.literal: Youwei fled, and Guangren was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei escaped; Guangren was arrested.

sentences.zh: 在獄言笑自若，臨刑猶言曰：「中國自強之機在此矣！」

translations.literal: In prison he talked and laughed as usual; at his execution he still said: "China's opportunity to strengthen itself lies here!"
translations.idiomatic: In prison he was calm and even cheerful; at the block he still said, "China's chance to strengthen itself lies in this!"

sentences.zh: 論曰：戊戌變法，德宗發憤圖強，用端棻等言，召用新進。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Wuxu reforms, Dezong roused himself to pursue strength, adopted the words of Duanfen and the others, and summoned new men for employment.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In the Wuxu reforms Emperor Dezong, determined to strengthen the state, took the advice of Li Duanfen and others and called in new men.

sentences.zh: 百日維新，中外震仰，黨爭遽起，激成政變。

translations.literal: For a hundred days the reforms made China and foreign countries tremble and look up in admiration, but factional struggle suddenly arose and provoked the coup.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred days the reforms awed China and the world, but factional struggle erupted and provoked the coup.

sentences.zh: 銳、光第、嗣同、旭及深秀、廣仁同日被禍，世稱「六君子」，皆悲其志。

translations.literal: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, Shenxiu, and Guangren suffered disaster on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, Shenxiu, and Guangren were executed on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.

sentences.zh: 內爭不已，牽及外交。

translations.literal: Internal strife did not cease, and foreign relations were drawn into it.
translations.idiomatic: Internal strife continued and entangled foreign relations.

sentences.zh: 其後遂釀庚子排外之亂，終致危亡。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Boxer uprising of 1900 was brewed, and in the end the dynasty was brought to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: This led to the Boxer uprising of 1900 and, in the end, ruin.

sentences.zh: 此亦代興衰一大關鍵也。

translations.literal: This too was a great turning point in the rise and fall of the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: This was a great turning point in the fate of the Qing dynasty.
